candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication discontinuation and client teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach safe discontinuation of sertraline using gradual dose reduction rather than abrupt cessation.

options.A: Yes; sertraline never produces discontinuation symptoms.
options.B: Yes; abrupt cessation is recommended whenever symptoms improve.
options.C: No; the dose should generally be reduced gradually when therapy is discontinued because abrupt stopping can produce a discontinuation syndrome.
options.D: No; sertraline must always be continued for life.

candidate.rationale: Sertraline labeling recommends gradual dose reduction rather than abrupt cessation whenever possible because discontinuation symptoms can occur.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sertraline should generally be tapered rather than abruptly discontinued because discontinuation symptoms may occur.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 2.6 Discontinuation of Treatment and 5.5 Discontinuation Syndrome
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
candidate.stem: A client who has taken sertraline for several months asks whether it can be stopped abruptly. Which response is best?
